body:
Lori, 2026-09-03, after fog landed: "It's impossible to see the fog - this would be useful to be able to turn on and off. Also, being able to watch a specific unit to see all of its state seems like a good idea." Plan file: C:\Users\lori_\.claude\plans\i-think-some-improvements-cached-shamir.md

THIS RESOLVES THE PARKED PAGES-VS-APP CALL in favour of the APP, on the criterion that item itself set (which is the better INSTRUMENT, not which is easier to share). See [[Move the replay pages to an app or a server rather than maintaining a second renderer]]. The web pages are not deleted and now diverge further -- known debt.

THREE DECISIONS LOCKED BY LORI:
1. The viewer runs the TACTICS WORLD LIVE, not trace playback.
2. The fog viewpoint CYCLES: observer -> side 0 -> side 1. Watching one fight from each side is how you catch a doctrine acting on knowledge it should not have.
3. The inspector is a WPF PANEL, not drawn on the map. MainWindow.xaml already states the precedent: "The status line is WPF chrome, not something the renderer draws. That decision is why IRenderer has no DrawText." WPF first, Raylib deliberately falls behind.
Plus: the rebindable key model is IN SCOPE for phase 1, because three new keys arrive and the parked item's own trigger was "when a third action arrives". See [[Rebindable key model for the viewer (no fixed keyset)]].

FOUR CONSTRAINTS THAT DECIDE THE DESIGN, found by graph and by explore agents:
- Nav.Viewer.Shared depends on Nav.Core ONLY, and the csproj says that absence IS the seam, "enforced by the compiler rather than by review". So health/rank/kit/target/sightings/fog are invisible to the viewer today. Phase 3 adds a NEW project Nav.Viewer.Tactics rather than widening the shared project's references, so the compiler-enforced claim survives.
- IRenderer has exactly FIVE verbs and ViewerAppTests.cs:731 fails if it grows a sixth. So no DrawText and no filled rect: the inspector is host chrome, and fog is a second TerrainImage (one texel per cell, exactly the right granularity).
- THE TWO RENDERERS DISAGREE ON ORDER. Raylib is immediate mode; D3D11 batches lines and circles and flushes them in EndFrame, so in WPF every line and circle lands ON TOP of every terrain quad whatever the call order. Fog must be terrain-class and drawn UNDER the units, which is the only arrangement both hosts agree on.
- Existing tests assert exact draw counts, so overlays must be OFF BY DEFAULT.

CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN FIRST DRAFT, both found by the explore agents rather than by me:
- The path overlay ALREADY EXISTS (ViewerApp.cs:387-411, sole selection, SkyBlue). But it draws CurrentPlans(), the PARTIAL reservation-window plan, and never surfaces IsPartial -- so a unit that planned only to the edge of its window reads as one that gave up. And line ~397 skips repeated cells, so a deliberate WAIT draws nothing, which is the exact "queued must not look like refused" trap ColourFor's own comment guards against. Those two gaps are the work; the polyline is not.
- ColourFor is static over AgentState and IGNORES Side, Alive and Away, all of which are already on the struct. Per-side colouring costs no new reference at all and makes the guard demo legible on its own.

ONE RETENTION CHANGE NEEDED IN NAV.TACTICS (phase 3): DemoWorld.TargetFor is private, called once from Fire, and the chosen target lives in a local list that goes out of scope. NOTHING STORES WHO A UNIT IS SHOOTING AT. Needs a Dictionary<int,int> written in Fire and exposed as TargetOf(int). Lori asked for "targeted enemy" explicitly.

NOT IN SCOPE, and each has a reason: Raylib presentation (deliberately behind; also its Upload is a per-pixel ImageDrawPixel loop, 262k calls on a 512x512 map, so a rebuilt fog texture is a real cliff there -- fix before picking Raylib back up). Reservation display (ReservationTable is internal with a private _byAgent and MovementSystem has no accessor; a unit's booked cells are reconstructable from its plan). Doctrine reasoning -- why a pad was chosen, why the reserve held a unit back, every gather-doctrine claim decision -- all computed and discarded every tick, and its own item.

WORKING MODEL CHANGED THIS SESSION. Lori: "We should think about using you as a controller instead of the implementer - this will allow the children to increase context without you doing so", and then "Even then it is possible to use a new agent to verify". So: I brief and dispatch implementer agents, dispatch a SEPARATE agent to verify, and keep the conclusions rather than the file dumps. Briefs must carry every decision explicitly, because a subagent shares none of the conversation.

PHASE 1 LANDED 2026-09-03 (uncommitted at time of writing): 644 -> 659 tests. InspectorRow + IViewerApp.Inspector, Keymap + PhysicalKey with defaults matching the old hard-coded bindings and hints GENERATED from the map, ViewerKeys gained Viewpoint=2048/PathOverlay=4096/LosOverlay=8192 bound to V/P/L, WPF inspector panel (fixed 260 wide, pinned out of the auto-size arithmetic), ColourFor now reads Side and Alive.
Verified cold by a separate agent: all nine constraints hold, five verbs intact, no Nav.Tactics reference, status-line invariance intact, exactly one existing test modified and not weakened.
TWO THINGS THE VERIFIER CAUGHT that the implementer's own report did not say: (1) the colour work has NO TESTS AT ALL -- both route fixes got one each, side/alive got none, including a rewrite of the hue spread that silently repaints every living unit; (2) "byte-for-byte unchanged" was true of the stuck/arrived/waiting branches but a FOURTH branch was inserted above them, so a dead-and-stuck unit now reads dark grey where it read red. The function's precedence changed even though those three branches did not. This is exactly why verification is worth a separate agent: the implementer's context made its own omission invisible to it.

DESIGN CORRECTION FROM LORI, and it kills my phase 2 design.
First, on the route overlay: I proposed colouring by IsPartial and marking every repeated cell. Building it proved both fire almost always -- group members read IsPartial continuously, and every solo plan opens with ~4 repeated cells while its search is in flight -- so neither carried information. Lori: "Keep those. I'm not interested in useless visual distinctions and those should be available in the panel view." So the MAP carries only distinctions that mean something (IsStuck for colour; a repeat while NOT Thinking for the wait marker, which is the genuinely-blocked case), and the raw facts (IsPartial, wait count) become inspector ROWS.

Second, and larger: "instead of exposing private data in odd ways? We can have an IDebugView on the things we care about (like agents, motion, or other) that when called dumps the current state as a dictionary."
This REPLACES the planned MovementSystem.Explain(agent) returning a bespoke AgentExplanation record, AND replaces the planned IUnitFacts in phase 3. One interface, implemented by anything worth watching; the panel renders whatever comes back, so new state appears in the inspector without the viewer changing.
THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST: put IDebugView in NAV.CORE and the viewer can read TACTICS state without referencing Nav.Tactics. DemoWorld implements the interface, the viewer consumes it as IDebugView, and the compiler-enforced seam in Nav.Viewer.Shared.csproj survives. That was the awkward part of phase 3 and it dissolves. Nav.Viewer.Tactics still exists but only as a composition root -- it CONSTRUCTS the tactics world; no data shape crosses it.
TWO AMENDMENTS I proposed and Lori has not yet objected to: return an ORDERED list rather than a Dictionary, because Dictionary has no contractual ordering and a panel whose rows reshuffle between frames is unreadable -- and the ordered shape is already InspectorRow(Group, Key, Value), so the panel needs no adapter. And STRINGS rather than object?, because the only consumer formats for display, boxing an int to unbox and ToString it buys nothing, object? invites production code to start reading it as data, and formatting at the source lets each type say how its own values should read (ticks until a gate lifts, not a raw tick number).
WHAT IDebugView DOES NOT SOLVE: the fog overlay needs CanSee(cell) per cell per frame. That is a query, not a dump, and stays its own small interface.

PHASE 1 FINAL SHAPE, 644 -> 671 tests, and the route overlay ended up almost the opposite of what I specified.
- Route colour: ONE colour. I specified IsPartial, measured it fires on nearly every grouped unit, switched to IsStuck, then found IsStuck can never reach the viewer at all -- see [[A unit that gave up is invisible: MovementSystem discards the stuck plan]] -- so the branch came out entirely.
- Wait marker: fires only on repeats PAST the plan's first real step. My !Thinking rule was wrong: the head repeats are latency pad written in at Commit time (AnchorTick = CurrentTick + Latency), so the search has already landed and Thinking is false when the plan is drawn. Head = the planner's own latency; interior = genuinely waiting for somebody.
- NEW SIGNAL, from Lori's "if there is no plan, isn't that information?": a cross on any unit absent from CurrentPlans() AND Alive AND !Arrived AND !Thinking. Drawn for every unit, not just the selected one, because the point is picking one out of a crowd.

THREE PIECES OF CODE THAT CANNOT CURRENTLY BE REACHED, and they are not the same case as each other:
1. RgbaColor.Orange as a route colour -- DELETED. No path to reachability without a Nav.Core change nobody has scheduled.
2. Colour by AgentState.Side -- KEPT, flagged speculative. ViewerSession.BuildWorld is the only place agents are created and both call sites pass side: 0; RecordedScenario has no side column and its parser rejects a five-token agent line. So `agent.Side * SideArcSpacing` can be deleted today without failing a test. It becomes live in PHASE 3 when the tactics world brings sides. Deleting and re-adding two dispatches later is churn; the difference from case 1 is a scheduled path, not a hoped-for one.
3. The Waiting-without-Stuck colour Rgb(150,150,170) -- PRE-EXISTING, not ours, and it never fires in the viewer. It needs RetryAfterTick > CurrentTick with StalledTicks == 0, and the only site that does that is GroupOps.Hold via MeteredGatherDoctrine; the viewer orders through the default scrum, so every waiting unit it can produce has stalled first and is caught by the Stuck branch above. Probed over ~1500 tick-samples across five fixtures. Stated as unreached in a comment rather than left as a silent hole.

A PREMISE OF MINE THAT WAS WRONG, corrected by the agent rather than by me: I told Lori a dead-and-stuck unit used to render red. Impossible -- MovementSystem.Remove sets StalledTicks = 0 AND Goal = Cell, and Stuck is !Arrived && StalledTicks > 0, so a corpse is always Arrived and never Stuck. The new dead branch overrides ARRIVED, not stuck: a body read 130,130,130 before and reads 55,55,60 now. The test pins that and asserts body.Arrived, so if Remove ever stops parking the goal the test fails rather than quietly testing something else.

REPO C:\repos\gamehub, branch main. git is NOT on PATH: "C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe". Build and test with mcp__janet__dotnet_check, target C:\repos\gamehub\GameHub.slnx. Plan file: C:\Users\lori_\.claude\plans\i-think-some-improvements-cached-shamir.md

COMMITTED THIS SESSION, oldest first, all green at each:
  e7bbdd2 fog: a side sees what its units can, and remembers what it cannot
  9efd616 a pad watches its own ground, demo enlarged to 49x33
  5e4b6d4 the replay prose says what the run actually did
  38e1812 the viewer says what one unit is doing, keys stop being welded on
  77d5d1a ask a unit what it is doing, and do not disturb it by asking
  0980551 the panel asks the movement layer instead of guessing from a snapshot
Tests: 644 at session start, 682 now.

IN FLIGHT when this was written: one implementer agent doing the READ-ONLY FIELD VIEW refactor. TryPeek comes OFF IDistanceFieldSource and onto a new read-only view interface that has no For, FieldCache implements both, MovementSystem's agent debug view takes the view. Modelled on IReservationView, which is the same pattern already in this codebase for the same reason. If its result is lost to the compact, check `git status` and `git diff` to see whether it landed.

NEXT, AND IT REVERSES A BRIEF OF MINE. Lori: "we should have the full list in the details window - we will do winnowing later, but the earlier we add things the easier they are." I had told an agent to drop debug rows that merely restated others; that was wrong. Restore as explicit rows: alive (not implied by a corpse's page shape), leader (even with no formation), stuck (even though derived from arrived+stalled), found and partial as TWO rows rather than one three-way "reach", last tick separate from the cell count, and the route preview back to the full remaining path rather than one cell. Add everything else reachable: LastPlanAttemptTick, LastVacancyWakeTick, WantsPlan, FieldKey, Latency, AnchorTick, the formation's slot ring, CellAt. Compute redundant rows from the same source rather than restating them, so winnowing stays cheap.
TWO THINGS THAT NEED NEW PRODUCTION API and are Lori's call, not mine: reservations (ReservationTable is internal with a private _byAgent, MovementSystem has no accessor, and IReservationView excludes HolderOf deliberately) and search progress while thinking (BudgetedSearch.Expanded/Finished are live but Agent.Search is internal, so a unit can only say "yes, searching").

THEN PHASE 3, four dispatches, one item each:
  1. TargetOf retention in DemoWorld. TargetFor is private, called once from Fire, and the chosen target lives in a local list that goes out of scope -- NOTHING STORES WHO A UNIT IS SHOOTING AT. Needs a Dictionary<int,int> written in Fire, exposed as TargetOf(int). Lori asked for "targeted enemy" explicitly.
  2. The seam. Lori's design: an IDemoWorldDebugView DERIVING FROM IDebugView -- inherit Describe(), add the queries the overlay needs (CanSee(cell), sightings, pads, target). DEFINE IT IN Nav.Viewer.Shared in primitives the viewer already speaks (cell ints, ticks), NOT in Nav.Core, because naming a Sighting or a kit would make Nav.Core learn what perception is, which the roadmap forbids. Nav.Viewer.Tactics is a new project that IMPLEMENTS it over DemoWorld -- an adapter, not a composition root that hands the viewer a DemoWorld. The mutable world never crosses the boundary. RIDER: Describe() is explicitly not a contract (nothing may branch on it, nobody may parse a value back), while CanSee IS relied on every frame -- the doc must say which members are which, or the inheritance implies they are the same kind of thing.
  3. Fog overlay + viewpoint cycling on ViewerKeys.Viewpoint (already bound to V). Observer -> side 0 -> side 1. Fog is a SECOND TerrainImage drawn after the terrain and BEFORE the units -- no sixth verb, one texel per cell, and it is the only ordering both hosts agree on, because D3D11 batches lines and circles and flushes them after terrain regardless of call order while raylib is immediate mode. Both renderers cache uploads by REFERENCE IDENTITY, so rebuild the fog image only when the visible set changes. Unseen enemies not drawn; remembered sightings as ghosts faded by CurrentTick - Sighting.Tick; unseen pads not drawn.
  4. LOS and weapon-range circles for the watched unit, from Kit.Sight and Kit.Range -- 6 vs 4 for a rifleman, 9 vs 5 for the scout buggy. Replaces the enemy ring the replay page lost when exposure-rank was retired. NOTE no wall-aware LOS exists anywhere: RadiusSight is octile distance, blind to walls on purpose, and there is no Bresenham in Nav.Core.

STANDING CONSTRAINTS FOR EVERY BRIEF: IRenderer has exactly five verbs and ViewerAppTests guards it. Nav.Viewer.Shared references Nav.Core ONLY. The status line's length is invariant and pinned. Overlays off by default -- existing tests assert exact draw counts. Every implementer mutation-checks its own tests. Ask what they could not do rather than accepting a silent workaround.

DELEGATION MODEL, see [[controller-not-implementer]]: one item per agent, a SEPARATE agent verifies cold against a numbered constraint list, and briefs must TELL the delegate to use razorgraph and janet because they do not inherit the habit.

COMMITTED e7557db "An instrument is handed a reference that cannot build a
field" -- 683 tests, zero warnings. TryPeek moved off IDistanceFieldSource onto
a new IDistanceFieldView with that one member and no For; FieldCache is its own
view the way ReservationTable is its own IReservationView; DebugFor passes
_fields.View. The narrowing is now a type, not a rule. New test
ThePanelReadsThroughAReferenceThatCannotBuildAField stands a source that throws
from For once the run is over. Residual, flagged and accepted: AgentDebugView is
nested inside MovementSystem, so an edit inside that one file can still name
system._fields; everywhere else the guarantee is the type.

IN FLIGHT: row exhaustiveness in AgentDebugView.Describe, per Lori's "we should
have the full list in the details window - we will do winnowing later". Restores
alive for the living, leader unconditionally, stuck as its own row, found and
partial split out of the three-way reach row, start/last tick split from the
cell count, the full remaining path as well as next, and CellAt(CurrentTick) as
"at now". Corpse page deliberately untouched -- Remove clears those fields, so
that is false data rather than winnowed data.

ENVIRONMENT: git is no longer on PATH in this shell. It lives at
"C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe"; prefix commands with
$env:PATH += ";C:\Program Files\Git\cmd".

STILL TO DISPATCH, one agent each, sequenced because two agents building the
same solution fight over obj/bin:
1. TargetOf retention in DemoWorld (TargetFor is private, called once from Fire,
   the chosen target goes out of scope -- nothing stores who a unit is shooting
   at, and "targeted enemy" was asked for explicitly).
2. IDemoWorldDebugView : IDebugView, declared in Nav.Viewer.Shared in
   primitives, implemented in Nav.Viewer.Tactics over DemoWorld. Nav.Viewer.Shared
   must keep its Nav.Core-only reference; the absence IS the seam.
3. Fog overlay as a second TerrainImage between terrain and units, plus
   viewpoint cycling on V (observer -> side 0 -> side 1).
4. Sight and weapon-range circles from Kit.Sight and Kit.Range for the watched
   unit.

AWAITING LORI: exposing HolderOf/reservations, and BudgetedSearch progress while
thinking. Both need new production API, so both are design calls, not mine.

Prose is part of the demo: the guard replay page must be rewritten from the
run's own trace once all of this lands, not before.

COMMITS since the last note:
- 007b9fc "The panel says every fact rather than the tidy ones" -- 689 tests.
  Row exhaustiveness per Lori's "full list in the details window". alive for the
  living, leader unconditionally, found/partial/stuck as three rows where reach
  was one, cells/start tick/last tick split, remaining path with an elision that
  reports how many cells it hid, and at now = CellAt(CurrentTick) beside the
  cell the unit stands on. Two viewer tests pinned old wording; each became two
  assertions. Corpse page untouched -- Remove clears those fields, so that is
  false data rather than winnowed data.
- 46bd695 "Ask an instrument, mechanically, what it can reach that changes
  state" -- 694 tests. [Observes] plus an IL walker in the test tree.

THE SPIKE'S FINDINGS, worth keeping:
- The code graph records Writes for field ASSIGNMENT only. Mutation through a
  reference (_visible[side] = seen) shows as Reads. Of Look()'s six mutations
  the graph sees one. Do not trust a graph-only purity audit.
- Owning the receiver is the whole difficulty. A linear IL scan loses the
  receiver at any branch, so a ternary inside an argument list gave fifteen
  false positives on the row builder. Fixed by merging the abstract stack at
  branch targets. Without that the ownership rule is worthless on real C#.
- Nav.Core is clean: ten instruments, 104 methods, 66 mutations dropped as
  owned, approved list EMPTY. Green is guarded by floors on methods-read and
  owned-dropped plus a control instrument that does mutate.
- Known holes, pinned as running tests: a delegate held in a field is invoked
  through Action.Invoke with no body and is missed (this codebase has that
  shape -- _deferred, Happened); a scratch list returned from a call reads as
  unknown provenance.
- Recommendation taken: do NOT build the analyzer. Prefer the structural fix (a
  view type with no verbs) and use the walk only where structure cannot reach.

DESIGN CALL MADE BY LORI: Look() gets a peek-only view for instruments, not a
tick-boundary resolve. My stated objection -- that a stale reading is a lie in
an instrument -- was backwards. The view shows what doctrine LAST ACTED ON, and
for an instrument whose purpose is watching a side act on limited knowledge that
is the more honest number; freshly-resolved perception would show the reader
knowledge the doctrine never had when it decided. Another entry for
design-partnership.

IN FLIGHT: IPerceptionView over DemoWorld, peek-only, DemoWorld its own view the
way FieldCache is. Doctrine path unchanged.

STILL TO DISPATCH, one agent each, sequenced (two agents building the same
solution fight over obj/bin):
1. Close the delegate hole in MutationWalk -- follow ldftn targets into a
   per-field delegate set. Cheap, and it is the one hole that matters here.
2. Audit Nav.Viewer.Shared with the walker. ViewerSession.DebugFor and
   ViewerApp's inspector are instruments by any reading. One ItemGroup, one test.
3. TargetOf retention in DemoWorld (TargetFor is private, called once from Fire,
   the chosen target goes out of scope -- nothing stores who a unit shoots at).
4. IDemoWorldDebugView : IDebugView, declared in Nav.Viewer.Shared in
   primitives, implemented in Nav.Viewer.Tactics over DemoWorld. Nav.Viewer.Shared
   keeps its Nav.Core-only reference; the absence IS the seam.
5. Fog overlay as a second TerrainImage between terrain and units, plus
   viewpoint cycling on V (observer -> side 0 -> side 1).
6. Sight and weapon-range circles from Kit.Sight and Kit.Range.

AT THE END, both required before this arc is done:
- Rewrite the guard replay page prose from the run's own trace and republish.
  Artifact 8376fd5c-3388-48bf-ac9c-51a4cf374dfa. Prose is part of the demo.
- ROADMAP.md is stale: header still says 632 tests, 3 September. Perception,
  the instrument work, and the Look finding all want entries. Do it once at the
  end rather than per commit.

COMMITS: 8f9623f (delegate following, 702), 3c4df67 (viewer audit clean, 704).

The viewer audits clean: nine instruments, 153 methods, 71 owned mutations
dropped, zero notes, approved list empty. Proof the walk crossed layers rather
than stopping at the seam: ViewerSession.DebugFor is one forwarding line yet
reports AgentDebugView's constructor writes, which live inside Nav.Core.

Delegate following closed the largest false negative. Nav.Core now reports ZERO
NOTES, which before was uninformative silence and now means no instrument
reaches an Invoke the walk cannot resolve -- neither Happened nor _deferred is
reachable from a marked member. Still missed and pinned as tests: a delegate
handed in as a parameter, and one held in a list (which is _deferred's shape).

TWO DECISIONS BY LORI:
1. [Observes] now means "reading changes nothing, FULL STOP" -- not the looser
   "does not change the simulation". Forced by InputAccumulator.Snapshot, which
   drains _keysPressed and _buttonsPressed as a side effect of being read, so a
   second caller silently gets nothing.
2. ViewerApp.Render gets marked. Widest read of the simulation in the viewer.

IN FLIGHT: the attribute's documented meaning tightened, Snapshot split into a
pure read (keeps the name, takes [Observes]) and a drain verb the hosts call,
callers updated in WpfHost, RaylibHost and ScriptedHost, Render marked.
InputAccumulatorTests has ~15 call sites and four pairs exist specifically to
pin the drain -- they follow the verb, not the read.

STILL TO DISPATCH, one agent each, sequenced:
1. TargetOf retention in DemoWorld -- TargetFor is private, called once from
   Fire, the chosen target goes out of scope; nothing stores who a unit shoots
   at, and "targeted enemy" was asked for explicitly.
2. IDemoWorldDebugView : IDebugView, declared in Nav.Viewer.Shared in
   primitives, implemented in Nav.Viewer.Tactics over DemoWorld. Nav.Viewer.Shared
   keeps its Nav.Core-only reference; the absence IS the seam. Note it should
   read through IPerceptionView, not DemoWorld's doctrine queries.
3. Fog overlay as a second TerrainImage between terrain and units, plus
   viewpoint cycling on V (observer -> side 0 -> side 1).
4. Sight and weapon-range circles from Kit.Sight and Kit.Range.

BANKED, not acted on: RepairCells is a public List<int> { get; } and both
RepairPointsFor and PeekRepairPoints hand back live references rather than
copies, while ByAgent copies. Pre-existing, mirrored deliberately.

AT THE END, both required: rewrite the guard replay prose from the run's own
trace and republish (artifact 8376fd5c-3388-48bf-ac9c-51a4cf374dfa), and update
ROADMAP.md, whose header still says 632 tests and 3 September.

COMMITS: 59988c2 (purity tightened, 705), 4712e76 (tick edge, 711).

THE MODEL, from Lori, now implemented for perception: the simulation is a
synchronous digital system. THE ONLY STATE YOU CAN SEE IS THE STATE AT A CLOCK
EDGE. A stop always lands at the end of a tick, so settling has finished before
anything can look. Established facts that fall out of it:
- Look() runs at the end of Settle and once from Listen; all six accessors are
  pure reads and all six are marked [Observes]. The observer effect is gone at
  the ROOT, not fenced behind a view -- which is why the doctrine-facing three
  audit clean too.
- IPerceptionView.AsOf is ONE number for the whole view. A clock edge makes
  every output valid together; three stamps would say three snapshots.
  Sighting.Tick is a different question (when that unit was last seen) and
  AsOf - Sighting.Tick is one side's staleness about one enemy.
- A tick spans TWO counter values. MovementSystem.cs:1161 has CurrentTick++
  two-thirds through Tick(): doctrine, leader election and the planning budget
  run at N; tables advance, units step and Happened fires at N+1. So at an edge
  CurrentTick is N+1 while the decisions that caused it were made at N.

[Observes] now means READING CHANGES NOTHING, FULL STOP -- not the looser "does
not change the simulation". Forced by InputAccumulator.Snapshot, which drained
the edge bits on read; Snapshot kept the innocent name and stopped causing,
Drain is the verb. ViewerApp.Render is marked and audits clean.

LORI'S CALL on the corpse finding: LEAVE IT. At an edge a unit killed during
Settle is still on the board as a hostile, because the demo removes the fallen
after Settle returns; 17 of 521 guard trace lines differ in the hostiles array
alone. Lori: "A corpse is on the board because that's known. We expect fog to
change things anyway." Chasing it would be chasing bit-identical outcomes in a
feature whose purpose is to change them.

FIFTH green-proving-nothing caught: _asOf stamped inside the stale+fog guard
passed all 101 tests. Nothing pinned that the clock advances on a quiet tick or
in a fog-free world.

IN FLIGHT: TargetOf retention in DemoWorld.

STILL TO DISPATCH, one agent each, sequenced:
1. RepairCells is public List<int> { get; } -- declared type wrong; and
   RepairPointsFor still hands back its live list while PeekRepairPoints copies.
   Lori: "Just because something is available doesn't mean someone should use
   it - but the notation should be right, no?"
2. IDemoWorldDebugView : IDebugView, declared in Nav.Viewer.Shared in
   primitives, implemented in Nav.Viewer.Tactics over DemoWorld. Must read
   through IPerceptionView, not the doctrine queries. Nav.Viewer.Shared keeps
   its Nav.Core-only reference; the absence IS the seam.
3. Fog overlay as a second TerrainImage between terrain and units, plus
   viewpoint cycling on V (observer -> side 0 -> side 1).
4. Sight and weapon-range circles from Kit.Sight and Kit.Range.

AT THE END: rewrite the guard replay prose from the run's own trace and
republish (artifact 8376fd5c-3388-48bf-ac9c-51a4cf374dfa), and update
ROADMAP.md, whose header still says 632 tests and 3 September.

COMMIT 1e0f37e: TargetOf retention, 717 tests, guard trace byte-identical. The
liveness filter is at the READ, not pruned in Fire -- exposure damage runs later
in Settle, so a map pruned at shot time would still name a unit killed after
firing.

LORI'S DESIGN CALL on how the viewer gets tactics facts: "So, the viewer gets a
list of idebugView items, no?" The viewer NEVER learns a tactics world exists.
Whoever composes the app hands it things that can describe themselves; it merges
their rows. Nav.Viewer.Shared keeps its Nav.Core-only reference, Nav.Viewer.Tactics
implements over DemoWorld, and the HOST references both and composes. The seam
holds because the viewer's ignorance is structural, not agreed.
Consequence: the interface must not name its implementer. IDemoWorldDebugView was
renamed mid-flight -- an interface in a project that cannot see DemoWorld must not
carry its name. Same mistake as HostilesFor reading like a question it was not.
Per-agent wrinkle: Describe() takes no args, so each item derives from IDebugView
(world rows) AND adds DebugFor(int agent) (the unit page). A source with nothing
to say about units returns an empty page.

SCENARIO: start with the guard scenario in the host, build purpose-made fixtures
later. Lori: "Seeing this already shows how some of the doctrine fails."

DOCTRINE FINDING, RECORDED AND EXPLICITLY NOT TO BE ACTED ON. Lori: the buggy
"gets killed going to a position no scout should finish going to after being hit
at all. It's a scout, and a heavy damage dealing weapon - it should be far more
cowardly." Two structural gaps behind it, neither a tuning problem:
1. Doctrine reads rank and health, never ROLE. The retreat table is rank-indexed;
   Kit carries Range, Sight, ShotsPerSecond, HitPoints -- all capability, no
   disposition. A buggy and a tank at equal rank and equal health fraction
   retreat at the same moment, and "this is the only pair of eyes on the map" is
   not a fact any doctrine can read.
2. A unit FINISHES what it was ordered to do. There is no abort-on-contact
   anywhere. That is the same absent idea as ROADMAP item 1 (a plan through fog
   should be tentative, corrected on contact), seen from the doctrine side
   instead of the planner side. Two symptoms, one missing mechanism.
Do NOT invent an economic rationale for a cowardice rule -- ask what the mechanic
is. See memory accelerate-advancement.

IN FLIGHT: the debug seam (renamed) plus Nav.Viewer.Tactics and its test project.

heading: HANDOFF, 2026-09-04, before a Claude Code update and restart
body:
STATE: main, 737 tests green, zero warnings, working tree clean at 8c48906.
Session went 644 -> 737 tests across fifteen commits.

COMMITS since the last note:
- aced37d  the debug seam. IWorldDebugView (Nav.Viewer.Shared, Nav.Core types
  only) derives from IDebugView and adds DebugFor(int agent). Renamed mid-flight
  from IDemoWorldDebugView -- an interface in a project that cannot see its
  implementer must not carry its name. DemoWorldDebugView in the new
  Nav.Viewer.Tactics implements it; reads perception through world.View only.
- 89335e7  ViewerApp takes IReadOnlyList<IWorldDebugView>? and merges. Order is
  movement layer, sources in supply order, Viewer group last. A colliding group
  heading is RENAMED (Unit (2)), never merged, never dropped. A throwing source
  loses its whole block and says so in one row after the viewer's own. A null in
  the list is refused at construction -- without that guard the broad catch turns
  a wiring bug into a permanent "threw NullReferenceException" row.
- 8c48906  Nav.Scenarios owns the guard scenario's construction; the demo keeps
  the clock, trace, narration and headline. Both traces and both replay pages
  hash identical. SendWave(int tick) is the seam for wave timing.

WHAT IS LEFT, one agent each, sequenced:
1. HOST COMPOSITION. Nav.Viewer.Wpf references Nav.Scenarios and
   Nav.Viewer.Tactics, builds GuardRetreatScenario, wraps its world in
   DemoWorldDebugView, hands it to ViewerApp as a source, and drives the
   scenario's clock. Nothing passes a source in production yet, so this is the
   step that makes all of aced37d and 89335e7 live. Nav.Viewer.Shared must keep
   referencing Nav.Core alone -- verify with a probe file naming DemoWorld in
   Nav.Viewer.Tests, which must still fail CS0234.
2. FOG OVERLAY. A second TerrainImage drawn after the terrain and before the
   units -- needs no sixth renderer verb and lands under the units in both
   hosts, which is the only ordering they agree on. Viewpoint cycles on V:
   observer -> side 0 -> side 1. Rebuild the image only when the visible set
   changes; both renderers cache uploads by REFERENCE IDENTITY. Existing tests
   assert exact draw counts, so overlays must be off by default.
3. SIGHT AND RANGE CIRCLES from Kit.Sight and Kit.Range for the watched unit.
   No wall-aware LOS exists -- RadiusSight is octile distance, blind to walls on
   purpose -- so this draws the radius really in force, and only becomes a real
   line-of-sight overlay when a LineOfSight : ISight lands.
4. GUARD REPLAY PROSE, rewritten from the run's own trace, and republished.
   Artifact 8376fd5c-3388-48bf-ac9c-51a4cf374dfa. HARD REQUIREMENT, see memory
   demo-prose-is-part-of-the-demo. Only once the work is done, never mid-change.
5. ROADMAP.md. Header still says 632 tests and 3 September. Wants: perception
   under the clock-edge model, the instrument work and [Observes], the seam, and
   the buggy finding under Known wrong.

BANKED, each its own item, none urgent:
- RepairCells is public List<int> { get; } -- declared type wrong. And
  RepairPointsFor still hands back its live list while PeekRepairPoints copies.
  Lori: "the notation should be right, no?"
- DemoWorld keeps no roster, so an unknown non-negative agent id gets answered
  with what the world knows rather than refused the way AgentDebugView refuses.
  Needs a membership accessor.
- The wave narration hard-codes "two rocket bikes, three riflemen, a buggy", a

- MutationWalk still misses a delegate handed in as a parameter, and one held in

- Nav.Core already has ScenarioFile/RecordedScenario for benchmark replays, so

ENVIRONMENT: the git-not-on-PATH workaround is no longer needed after a restart.
This shell predated Lori's git install today; a fresh session picks it up.

heading: 2026-09-03, close of day. DESIGN CALL, agreed, not yet built
body:
The composition gets an owner and it is a WORLD, not a scenario.

1. RENAME. GuardRetreatScenario is a world (grid + board + DemoWorld + squads +
   doctrine + wave schedule), not a scenario. Nav.Core already holds EIGHT
   scenario-named types (ScenarioAgent, ScenarioOrder, RecordedScenario,
   ScenarioOutcome, ScenarioRecord, ScenarioFile, ScenarioPlayback,
   ScenarioTrace) all meaning recorded movement data replayed. So:
   GuardRetreatWorld, project Nav.Worlds. Closes the banked name collision.

2. IWorld IN Nav.Core/Interfaces, beside IDebugView -- NOT in the world project.
   Members are Grid, MovementSystem Board, void Step(int tick): all Core nouns.
   In the world project it would be unholdable by ViewerSession, because
   Nav.Viewer.Shared references Nav.Core alone and a Worlds reference drags
   DemoWorld in transitively. IDebugView is the precedent: a Core interface Core
   defines for outside consumption. IWorld does NOT carry the debug view --
   reading and driving stay separate types.

3. Step(int tick) owns the seven-line tick currently inlined in
   GuardRetreatDemo.Play (tools/Nav.Demos/GuardRetreatDemo.cs:86-108):
   SendWave, guard.Advance, wave Advance, system.Tick, world.Settle, then
   remove world.Fallen. That ORDERING is a decision (the corpse finding lives in
   it). Two loops means the video and the trace are two simulations agreeing by
   coincidence, and findings come from traces. After this, Play keeps only
   narration and tallies, and the ordering becomes testable in the world's own
   tests rather than pinned only by whole-trace hashes.
   REVERSES the Nav.Scenarios.csproj comment "Nothing in this project writes
   output or advances a clock". Lori ruled on the reversal knowingly.

4. HELD, not rejected: ScenarioDefinition as data + Factory.Load(sd). Right
   destination, wrong week -- one definition makes a loader a constructor in a
   costume, and the file-format question compounds with ScenarioFile until the
   rename lands. Revisit at world two or three.

Also: THIS THREAD ITEM IS 263KB AND thread_show REFUSES TO PRINT IT. My own
handoff dumping did that. Keep additions short from here; a cursor beats a
transcript.

heading: Naming, to be revisited holistically
body:
NAMING, TO BE REVISITED HOLISTICALLY. Lori, on approving the world rename: "We may later revisit naming holistically." Not now, and not piecemeal -- the point is one pass over the whole vocabulary rather than another single rename.

What is already on the pile for that pass:

- DemoWorld is not a world. It is perception, combat, health and fog: the state a side reads and fights through. The GuardRetreatWorld rename exposed it, in the demo line "var world = guardWorld.World" -- a world holding a world. The local had to be called guardWorld precisely because "world" was taken by the thing with the weaker claim to the name.

- "Demo" prefixes types that are not about demos. DemoWorld and DemoTrace are used by the viewer, the tests and the worlds library; only Nav.Demos is actually a demo.

- Entered, on GuardRetreatWorld, was named by an implementer rather than chosen. It is the wave that arrived this tick, readable after Step. Arrived collided with AgentState.Arrived and Arrival with the private Arrivals schedule, so it is a name picked by elimination and should be looked at again.

- Scenario is settled and should stay settled: it means recorded movement data replayed, and Nav.Core owns eight types that say so. The 2026-09-04 rename moved the other meaning out to Nav.Worlds. Do not reopen this one.

heading: The root name, and where the viewer rule came from
body:
THE ROOT NAME, AND WHERE THE VIEWER RULE CAME FROM. Lori, 2026-09-04: "Nav is no longer what this is about - it says 'this is navigation' but it isn't", and then, on the missing separation level: "That's the source of the rule about the viewer, by the way."

THE GAP. Nav is doing two jobs: the product's namespace root and a claim about domain. There is no level above the projects that names the thing as a whole, so the top-level identity collapsed into what the bottom layer happens to do. Movement is the substrate, not the point, and the root says otherwise.

IT SHOWS UP TWICE, WHICH IS THE EVIDENCE IT IS REAL.

1. The product is not one of its layers. Nav.Core stopped being navigation some time ago and nothing said so: it holds IWorld, IDebugView and the group doctrine (GatherDoctrine, SettleWhereYouStand). "Core" is its own small lie -- it means "the important one", which is backwards.

2. The contract is not the bottom layer. Nav.Viewer.Shared references Nav.Core alone, and its csproj says the absence IS the seam. The STATED reason survives everything: a panel must not name a kit, a sighting or a health value, because an instrument that sees through fog makes fog meaningless. The MECHANISM does not. "Reference exactly one project" was free only while one project was everything; "the viewer references the bottom of the stack" is a fact about how deep the stack was when it was written, not a statement about what a viewer may know.

WHERE IT ALREADY BENT, AND WHO BENT IT. IWorld went into Nav.Core on 2026-09-04 because the reference rule left nowhere else to put it, and I wrote "it lives in Nav.Core, and the placement is the point" into its doc comment as though that were a derivation. It is not. An interface about worlds was pushed down into the movement layer to satisfy a constraint that counts projects rather than describing knowledge. The placement still works; the argument given for it was stronger than the argument available. That doc comment should be revisited in this pass, not defended.

THE RULE, REWRITTEN FROM THE PROPERTY. The viewer may name what is true of the BOARD and may not name what is true of a SIDE. Grid, cell, agent, plan, tick -- anyone watching sees those. Kit, sighting, health, target, fog -- those belong to somebody and must arrive through something that filters. This version says nothing about how many projects deep anything sits, so it survives the stack growing.

SEQUENCING. This is not "rename Nav". It is: re-derive the seam from the property, let the layers fall where that puts them, take the names out of the result. The rename is the LAST step. And it wants a session where nothing else moves -- yesterday's world rename was safe precisely because byte-identical traces were the only other thing in the diff.

The product name itself is Lori's and is not yet chosen. GameHub is available and the solution already carries it, but it reads like a repo folder rather than a thing. Do not pick one on their behalf.

Sketch only, subordinate to the re-derivation above: <Product>.Movement (was Nav.Core, Movement rather than Navigation because that layer also goes, arbitrates and reserves), <Product>.Tactics, <Product>.Worlds, <Product>.Viewer.*, <Product>.Demos, <Product>.Benchmark.

heading: The [rates] section is not read by anything
body:
THE [rates] SECTION IS NOT READ BY ANYTHING. Found 2026-09-04 while chasing an aside about composing doctrines. NOT ACTED ON -- reconciling it moves the fight, and the tuning call is Lori's.

THE THREE FACTS, EACH VERIFIED BY GREP OVER src/ tests/ tools/:

1. No production code reads damagePerSecond, selfHealPerSecond or repairPerSecond. The only readers anywhere are two assertions in tests/Nav.Core.Tests/WorldScaleTests.cs:139 and :141.

2. config/combat.ini opens that section shouting: "RATES ARE PER SECOND, NEVER PER TICK. A rate written per tick silently rescales the whole game when the tick changes, and the tick is one line of config/scale.ini away from changing. The loop multiplies by secondsPerTick." GuardRetreatWorld then passes repairPerTick: 0.03 and selfHealPerTick: 0.002 as literals -- the exact failure the comment forbids -- under a code comment claiming the values come from the config.

3. The numbers disagree. At secondsPerTick = 0.25, combat.ini implies repair 0.0875 and selfHeal 0.0125. The literals are 0.03 and 0.002: roughly 3x and 6x smaller.

A NEW SPECIES OF GREEN-PROVING-NOTHING, worth naming because it is subtler than the previous six. WorldScaleTests asserts selfHealPerSecond < damagePerSecond. That relationship is real and is reasoned about in the config's own comments -- a rate that can be overwhelmed, so a veteran under fire still needs a pad. The assertion is not vacuous. It simply does not hold the SIM to anything, because the sim never reads either number. A test guarding a file rather than a behaviour. The previous six were green while proving nothing; this one is green while proving something true about the wrong artifact.

WHAT IS NOT A JUDGEMENT CALL: whichever way this goes, the comment and the code must stop contradicting each other. Either the loop starts reading [rates] and the doctrine is retuned against the config's numbers, or the section admits it is documentation and the literals become the stated source of truth.

BEWARE WHEN FIXING: the guard demo's headline is a repair-rotation result (4 rotated through repair, worst overrun 0.20) and the retreat thresholds were tuned against 0.03. Changing the rate changes the fight, so both trace hashes move and the replay prose must be rewritten from the new run. That is a deliberate re-tune, not a bug fix, and it should be its own session.

ALSO UNCHASED, same constructor: exposureRadius: 6.0 is passed as a literal beside a comment saying "no exposure damage, because the enemy has weapons now". One of those two is stale. Not verified.

RELATED, from the same aside: the composition vocabulary is already mostly data. combat.ini carries armour classes, five weapons and four unit types; kits resolve by name via World.Enlist(id, "tank"); Ini tracks which keys fell back to defaults. What is hard-coded in GuardRetreatWorld is the ARRANGEMENT -- the map literal, eight start cells, the station, two pads, the attack station, the wave composition and its three arrival ticks, the retreat thresholds and the reserve. That is a smaller gap to a ScenarioDefinition than was assumed on 2026-09-03 when holding it was argued for.

heading: The renderer describes less than it can do
body:
THE RENDERER DESCRIBES LESS THAN THE THING BEHIND IT CAN DO, AND I DESIGNED TO THE DESCRIPTION. Lori, 2026-09-04, in three pushes, each correcting the same mistake. Agreed in principle, NOT STARTED, and deliberately deferred on budget.

HOW IT STARTED. Fog shipped drawing UNDER the units, with each drawable category filtered separately -- enemies not drawn, ghosts drawn instead, pads painted into the fog image. Lori: "Why does fog go UNDER units. IF it were applied over them then the only thing that matters is that you can't see the units. There's an argument for having a notional fog layer that limits how much we draw to the screen, but that's a different argument."

That is occlusion versus culling, and I had conflated them. Fog-over is ONE mechanism and it is complete. Fog-under is a rule per category, and every category added later needs someone to remember the rule. The reason I gave for under was a RENDERER FACT -- D3D11 batches lines and circles and flushes them in EndFrame, so shapes always land above terrain regardless of call order -- not a design preference. I presented a constraint as a choice.

THE THREE PARTS, ALL LORI'S, ONE IDEA.

1. SHAPES. "the solution to the problem of lines and circles (more circles than lines) is shapes... Aren't lines degenerate shapes?" Yes. Collapsing DrawLine and DrawCircle into one shape verb takes IRenderer from FIVE verbs to FOUR. I had been treating "a sixth verb fails a test" as a ceiling; the move is in the other direction. ViewerAppTests.TheRendererIsNeverAskedForAnythingBeyondTheFiveVerbs and the exact draw-count assertions move with it.

2. LAYER HEIGHT. "this may be used as 2d, but it is a 3d engine after all." Z makes ordering DATA rather than call sequence. That dissolves the hosts' disagreement instead of working around it: D3D11 sorts the batch it already has, nearly free; Raylib must buffer rather than issue immediately, which is the real cost of this part.

3. SHADERS. "And we have shaders..." A fog mask sampled in the pixel shader removes the layering argument entirely -- fog over units, correct, with no per-category filtering and no second TerrainImage. My claim that "the renderers cannot do translucent" was a fact about Viewer.hlsl AS WRITTEN, not about D3D11.

THE PATTERN, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THIS ENTRY. I treated the renderer as a fixed constraint three times running, and it is not fixed -- it is ours, and its description is narrower than its capability. Check that before designing around it again.

KNOWN COST, TO BE DECIDED DELIBERATELY. The shader route is WPF-only and widens the host gap. Raylib is already behind by choice (RaylibRenderer.Upload is a per-pixel ImageDrawPixel loop, 262k calls on a 512x512 map). Whether fog-as-shader is worth widening that gap is a call, not a detail.

STILL SHIPPED AND STILL WRONG UNTIL THIS LANDS: fog draws under units at 6613558, with the filtering described above. It works and it is legible; it is not the design.

heading: Narration: a scrolling event log, filtered by viewpoint
body:
NARRATION: A SCROLLING EVENT LOG, FILTERED BY VIEWPOINT. Chosen by Lori 2026-09-04 from three options, then HELD the same day -- "it's a big bite and more than I should try to sneak in". Nothing built. Decided, not started.

WHAT IT IS. A pane beside or under the map, newest last, scrollable so you can look back at what you missed. The shape Lori picked, verbatim from the option they chose:

  tick 320  wave 3 enters at (2,2)
  tick 341  guard 4 hit, health 0.41
  tick 344  guard 4 breaks off for pad (46,30)
  tick 352  attacker 17 destroyed by guard 2
  tick 358  guard 4 reaches pad, repairing
  tick 371  guard 2 promoted to veteran
  tick 389  guard 4 rejoins the line

THE STRUCTURE IS ALREADY DECIDED, AND NOT BY THIS CONVERSATION. MovementSystem.Happened is an event Action<MovementEvent> and MovementEvent's own doc comment says: "how a layer above learns where things are without reaching into the system or keeping a copy of its state. Every listener hears the same things in the same order. Fog of war is a listener that passes on only what a side could have witnessed." DemoWorld is already such a listener (DemoWorld.cs:705, system.Happened += Hear). So a viewpoint-filtered log is not a new argument -- it is the shape the project committed to before fog existed.

THE LOG MUST ANSWER TO THE VIEWPOINT, and this is the whole reason it is not a trivial feature. Watching as side 1 and being told "guard 2 promoted to veteran" leaks precisely what 6613558 spent a commit hiding. Narration is a filter on the stream, exactly as fog is a filter on the stream. Build it that way from the first line or it will have to be retrofitted.

THE GAP. The vocabulary is movement-only: MovementEventKind is Added, Moved, Removed. The tactics layer has NO broadcast. DemoWorld.Fallen is a per-tick snapshot cleared at the head of the next Settle, not a stream. So this wants a second broadcast at the tactics layer mirroring the Core one -- and mirroring its ordering guarantee, because a log whose lines reshuffle between runs is not an instrument.

WHY BROADCAST RATHER THAN DIFFING. The alternative is the viewer comparing state frame to frame and inferring what happened. That requires the viewer to keep a copy of tactics state, which is the exact thing the seam forbids. Recommended without asking, because the codebase's own written principle already answers it.

THE EXPENSIVE HALF, FLAGGED BEFORE IT STARTS. Four of the seven lines are movement or combat facts and come nearly free. Two are DOCTRINE DECISIONS -- "breaks off for pad" and "rejoins the line" -- and the design-audit item already records that doctrine reasoning (why a pad was chosen, why the reserve held a unit back, gather-doctrine claim decisions) is computed and DISCARDED every tick. Nothing survives to broadcast. Making the doctrine announce what it decided is a change to the doctrine, not a listener bolted on afterwards.

That is also where the value is. A log of moves and deaths is a feature; a log that says why a unit broke off is the instrument that shows a doctrine acting on knowledge it should not have had. Worth doing properly, which is why it was not sneaked in.

heading: AGENT and UNIT: the first name the pass actually settles
body:
"UNIT (2)" IN THE PANEL, AND THE FIRST NAME THE NAMING PASS ACTUALLY SETTLES. Lori, 2026-09-04, seeing the rebuilt inspector for the first time: "why are there two units shown". Decided: AGENT for the movement layer, UNIT for the tactics layer.

WHAT THEY WERE LOOKING AT. Two debug views both call their group "Unit" -- MovementSystem.AgentDebugView (id, side, cell, goal, arrived) and DemoWorldDebugView.UnitDebugView (id, side, health, armour, rank, contribution, exposed). ViewerApp de-collides them by renaming the second, and its comment says exactly why: "A source is free to call a group anything, and 'Unit' is the likeliest name in the codebase for it to pick -- so without this a tactics world's unit rows would land under the movement layer's own heading and read as the movement layer's answers."

So the MECHANISM is right and stays. What was wrong is that "(2)" tells a reader nothing, which is precisely the reaction it got. The fix belongs at the two sources, not in the panel.

WHY AGENT. Not invented for the panel: the movement layer already uses it throughout -- MovementSystem.Agent is the type, AgentState is the per-tick snapshot, DebugFor takes an agent id, AddAgent places one. The heading now says what that layer has always called the thing. UNIT is then unambiguously the thing that fights, and the tactics side changes nothing.

This is worth noting as the first name the holistic naming pass has actually SETTLED rather than banked, and it settled from evidence (what the layer already calls itself) rather than from taste. That is the method the pass should use for the rest.

FOUND UNDERNEATH IT, HELD DELIBERATELY: id and side are reported TWICE, once by each layer, for the same unit, and nothing checks the two answers agree. Lori's call was to leave it and look at it in the naming pass with everything else. Two options were on the table and both are still open: drop them from the tactics view, since the movement layer owns the roster (it is where an agent is added, given a side and removed); or keep both and add a test that the layers agree, turning an accidental redundancy into a deliberate cross-check. Do NOT quietly pick one while doing something else.

Also worth carrying into that pass: the panel is what made this visible. Two layers answering the same question about the same unit was invisible while the rows were one flat monospace block, and obvious the moment they sat under two headings. The instrument found it, which is the argument for the instrument.
